title: Engineer-Facing Rapid Battle Brief (draft)
content:
Purpose and audience

This is a compact, engineer-facing battle brief intended for SEs and platform engineers who need a fast technical narrative for pilots and discovery calls. Treat it as a single-sheet reference (with callouts for demos and pilot handoffs). Not a polished deck yet — rough talking points, triage heuristics, and a short pilot checklist.

Current status
- Draft: needs security bullet and Dedicated throughput numbers verified by infra team (see open questions).
- Suggested use: 5–10 minute pre-call prep, emergency quick reference during technical discovery.

Topline positioning (30s)
- Redwood gives predictable, production-grade inference across hosted, dedicated, and private footprints.
- For platform teams: same API surface, consistent SLAs, and explicit cost/latency levers (batching, KV cache, model variants).

Persona callouts
- Integration Architect / Platform Engineer: cares about latency SLOs, regional routing, private networking (VPC), and onboarding effort.
- ML Engineer: cares about quality regression risk, model versioning, and eval pipelines.
- SRE / Infra: cares about autoscaling behavior, observability hooks, and safe fallbacks.

Key technical hooks (talking bullets)
- Unified API: one SDK and REST interface for hosted, dedicated, and private—customer code unchanged when you move to reserved capacity or on-prem.
- Deterministic latency controls: configurable routing policies + model variants for graceful degradation (example: route 80% to L2 low-latency quantized model, 20% to high-fidelity model for QA).
- Cost levers: prefix/KV caching, micro-batching heuristics, and quantization profiles with measured quality deltas.
- Observability: per-token latency and token-cost breakdowns, per-route error rates, and automatic regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.

Quick demo script (3 min tech demo)
1) Start with console: show model catalog and performance profile for an open model (filter by region, latency, and token-rate).
2) Show a route config: how to pin a model version and add a fallback variant.
3) Trigger a sample request and inspect trace: token-level timing, model fallback event.
4) Show cost breakdown for a sample conversation (token counts, cache hits).

Objection responses — technical
- "We can host our own model cheaper": if they own HW, agree but highlight operational delta: batching/KV cache + kernel selection maturity drive 30–60% cost per usable request reduction in our benchmarks for real workloads. Offer to run a short micro-benchmark with their prompt set.
- "Latency spikes with batching": explain continuous batching with SLO-aware cutoff, and show how to configure max latency and batching window. Mention sample configs and a PR link.
- "Data residency / compliance": Redwood Private supports VPC control plane and on-prem package; mention KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. Link to security checklist (TODO add link).

Canary and fallback plan (engineer checklist)
- Canary goals: verify 95th-p latency, observe error-rate, validate rollback path.
- Canary config: 5% traffic to new model, 1-minute warmup, 30-minute observation window.
- Metrics to watch: 95th-p latency by route, token-cost variance, model error spike (NLP hallucination rate via eval prompts).
- Rollback triggers: latency > SLA by 20% for 5 consecutive mins OR error-rate > baseline + 3x.

Pilot kickoff checklist (short actionable items)
- Pre-call: collect sample prompt set (top 50), target SLOs, peak QPS, and expected concurrency.
- Day 0: create customer workspace, upload prompts, run baseline eval (30 min).
- Day 1–3: run canary with production traffic shadowing; instrument traces into their APM.
- Success criteria: <SLO breach for 48 hours AND <10% quality regression on eval prompts.

Suggested performance numbers (need infra verification)
- Medium workload example: 100 rps, avg seq len 256 tokens, expected 95th-p latency ~120–220 ms on Dedicated-1 (T4-like) with continuous batching enabled (TBD).
- Cost guidance: caching + batching can reduce token unit cost by up to ~40% for chat-like traffic patterns in our tests — save figure pending detailed run.

Tactical play snippets (copyable)
- Rapid qualifier script: "Are you testing inference for end-user facing experiences (chat/assist) or internal batch jobs? What are your top 3 SLAs (p50, p95, error budget)?"
- Dev handoff note: "Upload 50 representative prompts and enable prefix cache for 24 hours — we’ll return a heatmap of token reuse and suggested cache TTLs."

Known gaps and open questions (TODO)
- Security copy: need approved language for FedRAMP/ISO claims for customer-facing one-pager. Owner: Priya.
- Precise Dedicated throughput numbers per instance type for common models (Llama-like, OPT-family). Owner: Diego — ping infra.
- Example pricing band for reserved capacity pilots (need finance input). Owner: Owen.

Internal references and links
- Onboarding guide (internal): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/engineer-onramp
- Recent infra perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/278
- Slack thread on fallback heuristics: #se-fallbacks (link to message pinned in channel)

Notes to self (copyedit stage)
- Replace placeholders with exact latency/cost numbers before se enablement workshop on Feb 20.
- Add one short security FAQ (3 bullets) and an example legal/data flow diagram.
- Convert to slide deck: 6 slides — top-level pitch, technical hooks, demo script, canary checklist, objections & counters, pilot pricing.

Appendix: sample minimal config snippet (talk track friendly)
- "Route A: model=redwood/llama-q8-1, weight=80, max_latency=200ms; Route B: model=redwood/llama-v2, weight=20, max_latency=400ms; Cache: prefix_ttl=300s"

End.
